Hello Ryan,

Thank you for reaching out to S-Docs Support.

The problem you outlined is a known limitation of lineitems queries. If there are multiple present in a template with different where clauses they will all use the last where clause. To avoid this you will need to convert your queries into lineitemsSOQL (aka Direct SOQL) queries, which is outlined in the following article:

https://www.sdocs.com/resources/documentation/using-s-docs-direct-soql-feature-for-related-list/

Let me know if you have any other questions.

Cheers,

Santiago Uribe Guiza
Support Engineer
S-Docs for Salesforce

Hello Matthis,

After taking a look and doing some testing, it seems that you are simply running into the 20 page limitation for DOCX templates.
https://www.sdocs.com/knowledge-base/sdocs/understanding-template-formats/s-docs-limitations/#upper-limits

Given that you only have two pages with dynamic content, you may want to place the other 18 pages into a component template and then call your component template in the original.
https://www.sdocs.com/knowledge-base/sdocs/creating-templates/create-component-templates/

However, the above solution, while it may enable you to upload, will probably lead to you encountering the same error when you generate. Given that you are still hitting this limitation, you may need to either shorten the docx file (pages is the relevant limitation rather than file size) or recreate your template as a PDF template.

Best,
George Gilfond

Hi Dave,

Thanks for reaching out about this issue. The first thing that I noticed is that you have two doclist parameters in your button code. The doclist parameter is a comma delimited list and should only be in there one time. EX: doclist='NOGA - Notice of Grant Award, S-Docs NOGA Email Template'

Second, the sendemail parameter is meant to be a 1 or a 0 and not a template. You should change it to be sendemail=1.

Please make those updates to the template and let me know if you are still having the issue.

Here is documentation on the button parameters as well for reference: https://www.sdocs.com/knowledge-base/sdocs/generate-documents-automatically/parameters-for-apex-buttons-calls-to-create-s-docs/#:~:text=send%20an%20email.-,sendemail%3D,-1%20to%20enable

Hello Morgan,

Thanks for reaching out to S-Docs support. Yes, you can place conditional logic around the document section based if no records show.

The simplest route I typically suggest is to leverage a named query to collect the count of records and place it into a merge field.

You can use the same merge field within the render to conditionally display the component if the value is more than 0.

Example:


<!---->

<!--RENDER=  > 0 -->

COMPONENT

<!--ENDRENDER-->

I leveraged the two articles to accomplish this goal.

https://kb.sdocs.com/knowledge-base/sdocs/related-lists-and-soql-queries/the-named-query-feature/
https://kb.sdocs.com/knowledge-base/sdocs/applying-logic/overview-conditional-logic/​​​​​​​

Feel free to reach out if any questions arise.

Cheers,


Kiel VanTiem
Support Director, S-Docs

Hello Anderson,

The issues here could very likely be due to a small Salesforce limitation. Unfortunately, Salesforce does have trouble with Visualforce pages on mobile devices (Android and iOS). They do offer methods of creating Visualforce pages that can work on mobile and desktop, though that does take some effort to build: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.pages.meta/pages/vf_dev_best_practices_pages_multipurpose.htm

That said, we also offer alternatives. With our SDK options, and some flows, you can do just about everything. Our knowledge base has a ton of options that can be leveraged to work around some Salesforce limitations like this.

Regards,
